# Curriculum Map

Twenty-four modules plus pre-work over six terms. Each module has a micro-level guide (outcomes,
week-by-week time-boxed session plans, labs, assessment, common mistakes, readings, instructor
notes) in [`curriculum/`](../curriculum/README.md), and runnable labs built on the course library
[`cfmat`](../cfmat).

## How the terms build

**T1 Foundations.** Market plumbing (M01) and macro context (M02); the tools of the trade — Python
(M03), statistics with multiple-testing discipline (M04) and research-grade data (M05). Ends with
Review 1, the Term 1 exam and Bootcamp 1.

**T2 Analysis and Derivatives.** Technical indicators and patterns tested as hypotheses (M06);
fundamentals and factor research (M07); pricing and the Greeks (M08); second-order Greeks,
futures curves and option structures (M09).

**T3 Strategy Research.** The main strategy families (M10), honest backtesting (M11), and the
Strategy Studio — screener, rule-based Strategy Creator, trade-level backtester, F&O signals and
parallel optimisation (M12). Ends with Review 2, exam 2 and Bootcamp 2 (trading-floor simulation).

**T4 Risk, Portfolio and Trading Systems.** Risk and sizing (M13), portfolios of assets and of
strategies (M14), microstructure and execution (M15), market-data handling (M16), the trading
platform and SEBI's framework (M17), and monitoring and n8n automation (M18). Capstone topics are
approved in Week 38.

**T5 AI for Trading.** Machine learning without leakage (M19), deep learning (M20), reinforcement
learning (M21), NLP, LLMs and RAG (M22), and advanced strategies with hyperparameter optimisation
and overfitting control (M23). The capstone track runs alongside (pre-registration in Week 40).
Ends with Review 3, exam 3 and Bootcamp 3.

**T6 Capstone and Career.** Four weeks of paper trading under limits, ethics, the career studio and
Demo Day (M24).

## Teaching approach

- **Live weekends** for concepts and cases; **clinics** for labs with TAs; **office hours** and a **quiz-and-peer-review** hour each week.
- **Labs are plain Python** (Jupytext percent format): run as scripts or open as notebooks. Every lab runs offline on synthetic or fictional data with *planted, documented effects*, so learners can see a method work when the effect exists — and see it fail when it does not.
- **Peer code review** through GitHub pull requests in every module.
- **Cases** from Indian market episodes use data at least three months old and are never framed as recommendations.
- **Guest practitioners** each term from prop desks, AMCs, brokers, exchanges and regtech.

## Core texts

- John C. Hull, *Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives*
- Ernest P. Chan, *Quantitative Trading* and *Algorithmic Trading*
- Marcos López de Prado, *Advances in Financial Machine Learning*
- Stefan Jansen, *Machine Learning for Algorithmic Trading*
- Yves Hilpisch, *Python for Finance*
- Larry Harris, *Trading and Exchanges*

Supplementary: Natenberg, *Option Volatility and Pricing*; Narang, *Inside the Black Box*; Aronson,
*Evidence-Based Technical Analysis*; Cartea, Jaimungal and Penalva, *Algorithmic and
High-Frequency Trading*; Grinold and Kahn, *Active Portfolio Management*; Tsay, *Analysis of
Financial Time Series*; Sutton and Barto, *Reinforcement Learning*; Tunstall et al., *NLP with
Transformers*; Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*; Ilmanen, *Expected Returns*;
NISM Series VIII and XV workbooks. Module-specific papers are listed in each module guide.
